subject: MedSync CPRA role & subprocessor handoff plan
messages:
From: Laura Espinoza <laura@medsync.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@medsync.com
Date: Sat, 27 Dec 2026 16:11:00 -0800
Subject: CPRA classification & subprocessors — follow up

Alex — thanks for the demo earlier. Two quick asks as we move toward contracting for the pilot:

1) Can you confirm Redwood's position under CPRA/CCPA for this use case — are you signing as a 'service provider' (limited-use) or do any aspects of the integration trigger a 'processor' classification? MedSync needs firm language for our procurement team.

2) We need the current subprocessor list and a high-level explanation of how data may transit between cloud providers (we run in us-west but have regulatory restrictions on certain workflows). If a subprocessor change requires onshore fallback, what options do you provide (e.g., Dedicated pools, Private deployment, or other onshore-only controls)?

If you can send a redline of the DPA and a CSV of subprocessors, we can run this through legal tomorrow.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Espinoza
Head of Legal Operations | MedSync Health
laura@medsync.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Espinoza <laura@medsync.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Dec 2026 18:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CPRA classification & subprocessors — follow up

Thanks Laura — looping in Monica (legal) and Grace (privacy) to confirm. Quick summary from my side so procurement has what you need:

- Redwood's default stance for SaaS-hosted inference is to act as a "service provider" under CPRA/CCPA for customer-configured workloads: limited-use, no sale of personal information, and we process only per customer instructions. That holds for hosted API and Dedicated pools.

- For customers requiring onshore-only handling we offer two clear paths: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in a US region) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package). Both support contractual data residency and onshore fallback.

- Subprocessors: primary infra providers (AWS, GCP), observability vendors (log aggregation), and a small number of model optimization partners. We maintain a live inventory and provide 30-day notice for subprocessor additions with the ability to object per standard DPA terms.

I'm attaching the DPA redline and our current subprocessor inventory CSV for your review (see attachments). Monica/Grace — could you confirm the framing above and propose any contract language changes we should send back?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

Attachments: MedSync_DPA_Redline_20261227.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_inventory_20261227.csv (csv)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Espinoza <laura@medsync.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CPRA classification & subprocessors — follow up

Laura / Alex — quick legal note after reviewing the redline:

- Confirmed: Redwood accepts Service Provider classification for the described pilot. We will sign a DPA with limited-use language and an explicit non-sale clause.

- Subprocessor controls: we propose the following contractual commitments for MedSync's DPA:
  * Maintain current inventory (attached CSV) and provide no less than 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors that will process MedSync personal information;
  * For any new subprocessor located outside the US that would materially affect data residency for regulated workflows, Redwood will offer either an onshore fallback path (Dedicated/Private) or a documented mitigation plan;
  * Right to object: MedSync may object to a new subprocessor within the notice period; if we cannot remediate, we will provide a mutually agreed transition plan (typically 30–60 days).

- Evidence: to close procurement items, we can provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, KMS key-handling summary (we do not hold customer keys for hosted by default, but integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated/Private), and a short dataflow diagram showing ingress → inference → ephemeral KV cache → telemetry/metrics exporters. I'll prepare the artifacts and send as separate attachments.

A couple of open redline points we flagged for MedSync:
  1) Add explicit onshore fallback language tied to regulated workflows (suggested clause in paragraph 7.3 of the redline).
  2) Clarify 3rd party model provider usage — we can commit to naming model providers in the subprocessor inventory or provide a class-based disclosure ("model providers: inference-hosting partners").

If that aligns with MedSync, Alex — can you confirm and send back a one-page summary to procurement so they can circulate?

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Laura Espinoza <laura@medsync.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CPRA classification & subprocessors — follow up

Monica / Alex — this is helpful and aligns with our procurement needs. A few confirmations before we circulate to the buying committee:

1) MedSync accepts Redwood's service provider classification and non-sale representation.
2) 30 days' notice for subprocessor additions is fine; we do want the right to object for onshore-restricted workflows.
3) For model-provider naming: class-based disclosure is acceptable for now (we'll ask for names if we enter production with regulated datasets).

Please send the SOC 2 excerpts, the KMS key-handling note, and the short dataflow diagram. We'll complete our internal review and route the DPA for signature — I'll send a DocuSign in the next step.

Appreciate the quick turnaround over the holidays.

Laura
